context.guidance: Serialise only the fields a response needs, using explicit allow-lists or response shapes rather than whole models or nested records. Remove Personal Data Elements the requester is not entitled to see, so each response stays within the Purpose for which the data was collected under §6(1). Apply the same field limits on every route that returns the same record, as Rule 6(1)(b) requires for access control.

value.fix: Replace the deny-list (`exclude: ['password', 'totpSecret']`) with an explicit allow-list of the fields the response actually needs, for example `{ name: 'User', include: ['id', 'displayName', 'avatarUrl'], model: UserModel }`, or map records through a dedicated response DTO/serializer (e.g. `toPublicUser(user)`). A deny-list automatically exposes any new column added to UserModel later (email, phone, address, recovery codes, reset tokens, session data, internal flags). Set up separate response shapes by requester: a public/other-user shape with minimal identifiers, and a self/admin shape that adds fields like email only when the caller is entitled to them. Apply the same allow-list on every route and nested relation that returns a User, including populated or joined records inside other models, list/search endpoints and admin exports, so field limits stay consistent. Make sure secrets (password hash, totpSecret, tokens) can never be returned on any path, for example with `select: false` / `defaultScope` at the model layer. Add tests that check each User-returning endpoint's response contains exactly the allowed keys.
